claims.statement: A clinically suspicious anal lesion requires representative lesion tissue for diagnosis.
claims.limitation: Independent clinical review of this exact claim and its application is pending.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: A biopsy result applies to the tissue sampled; an unsampled palpable lesion still requires evaluation.
claims.limitation: The wrong-site fictional specimen comparison is an author application of lesion-directed assessment, not a quantified biopsy-sensitivity claim.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Pelvic MRI assesses primary anal-cancer extent and pelvic nodes for treatment planning.
claims.limitation: Independent clinical review of this exact claim and its application is pending.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Thoracic and abdominal CT assess distant spread; a low-dose PET localization acquisition is not equivalent to diagnostic staging CT.
claims.limitation: PET/CT is complementary. The constructed acquisition log explicitly identifies which CT protocol was performed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Inguinal lymph-node involvement is regional nodal disease in anal squamous cancer.
claims.limitation: Independent clinical review of this exact claim and its application is pending.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Definitive chemoradiation is the usual curative pathway for nonmetastatic anal-canal squamous cancer.
claims.limitation: Selected very early lesions are exceptions; this claim is applied to a bulky node-positive primary, not a superficial excision candidate.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Concurrent fluorouracil and mitomycin with radiation is an established anal-cancer chemoradiation regimen.
claims.limitation: Alternative regimens exist; no dose, toxicity-based substitution or radiation schedule is ranked.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Abnormal anal screening results warrant HRA assessment with directed biopsy for histologic confirmation in adults with HIV.
claims.limitation: Independent clinical review of this exact claim and its application is pending.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Normal digital examination does not exclude flat anal HSIL detectable with HRA.
claims.limitation: Independent clinical review of this exact claim and its application is pending.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: HSIL is intraepithelial neoplasia; stromal invasion establishes an invasive rather than solely intraepithelial lesion.
claims.limitation: Independent clinical review of this exact claim and its application is pending.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Treating biopsy-confirmed anal HSIL reduces anal-cancer progression in adults with HIV.
claims.limitation: ANCHOR supports treatment versus monitoring in adults with HIV aged at least 35; sources discussing that trial are not counted as different trials. No extrapolation to all risk populations.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with HIV and biopsy-confirmed anal HSIL.

claims.statement: Office-based hyfrecation is a reasonable initial treatment for accessible anal HSIL in adults with HIV.
claims.limitation: NIH supports this approach; ANCHOR did not establish superiority over other effective HSIL treatments. No ranking among otherwise eligible topical and ablative modalities.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: NYSDOH recommends HRA six months after successful treatment of anal HSIL.
claims.limitation: Single adequate guideline supports this exact six-month recommendation (A3). It is not a universal proven optimal surveillance interval.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with HIV after anal HSIL treatment.

claims.statement: A new palpable anal lesion after HSIL treatment requires lesion-directed evaluation despite reassuring screening cytology.
claims.limitation: This is a symptomatic lesion-evaluation decision, not an empirically established negative-test threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Small, well-differentiated, node-negative anal-margin cancers may be treated by margin-negative local excision without sphincter injury.
claims.limitation: Limited comparative evidence. The drafted favorable lesion is wholly skin-based; an exact minimum margin is not taught and adequate proposed clearance is deliberately beyond disputed boundaries.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Poorly differentiated anal-margin squamous cancer is unsuitable for a local-excision treatment pathway.
claims.limitation: SEOM directly names poor differentiation; ASTRO summary supports selected excision only without higher-risk histology but supplies no granular threshold. Clinical ranking requires review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Suspected residual or recurrent anal cancer should be confirmed histologically before radical salvage surgery.
claims.limitation: Independent clinical review of this exact claim and its application is pending.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Resectable local anal-canal recurrence after chemoradiation without distant spread is a standard indication for salvage APR.
claims.limitation: Multidisciplinary review and an achievable complete resection matter; reirradiation and systemic approaches have selected roles, not blanket exclusion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Isolated inguinal nodal recurrence in a previously irradiated groin can be managed with inguinal node dissection.
claims.limitation: Recommendation is drawn from specialist consensus and limited data; no dissection extent, wound reconstruction, survival estimate or universal reirradiation prohibition is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: FDA approved retifanlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel for first-line inoperable recurrent or metastatic anal-canal squamous cancer.
claims.limitation: Same regulatory evidence, not two independent trials. A supported US option among the offered regimens; complete individualized oncology eligibility is outside the question.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Retifanlimab monotherapy has an FDA indication after platinum progression or intolerance in recurrent or metastatic anal-canal squamous cancer.
claims.limitation: Do not confuse earlier fluorouracil?mitomycin radiosensitization with progression on platinum therapy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Response may continue through 26 weeks from chemoradiation initiation when there is no progression.
claims.limitation: WITHHELD from scored use. SEOM response section uses treatment initiation, while another follow-up paragraph says after therapy; preserve the clock discrepancy and the owner eight-week hold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Documented progression during post-chemoradiation response assessment warrants prompt evaluation and biopsy.
claims.limitation: Only a boundary for the unkeyed owner hold; no new fixed biopsy interval is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Society guidance differs on adequate anal-margin excision clearance and management of close margins.
claims.limitation: WITHHELD: SEOM discusses greater than 1 mm histologic clearance; older US ARS discusses greater than 1 cm adequate clearance and re-excision. These are not silently equated, averaged or taught as a universal threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: Persistent oncogenic HPV contributes to anal squamous neoplasia; HIV modifies risk rather than serving as the causal virus.
claims.limitation: Fresh independent fact check does not alter or broaden the exact 2026-08-31 approvals.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia scenario.

claims.statement: An epithelial-only specimen cannot establish absence of invasion in unsampled underlying lesion tissue.
claims.limitation: Application of representative-lesion biopsy and specimen logic, not a quantified sensitivity/depth rule. The biopsy and block inventory in the draft are constructed observations.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia review-response drafts.

claims.statement: Endoanal ultrasound is limited by a stenotic canal and has less regional anatomic coverage than pelvic MRI.
claims.limitation: One adequate specialist imaging review directly supports the ultrasound limitation; current SEOM independently supports pelvic MRI for local extent. No exact canal diameter or tumor-size cutoff is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia review-response drafts.

claims.statement: HRA delineates flat anal epithelial lesions more precisely than standard anoscopy.
claims.limitation: Current federal guideline explicitly distinguishes these acquisitions. This is not a universal algorithm for every cytology/HPV combination.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia review-response drafts.

claims.statement: Locoregional perianal SCC outside the selected favorable local-excision group is treated with a chemoradiation pathway.
claims.limitation: Applied to initial treatment of a still-present poorly differentiated lesion. Does not infer a postoperative adjuvant recommendation after wide complete excision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the constrained anal-neoplasia review-response drafts.
